write_policy.rule: All non-production AgentOS development must explicitly target the integration branch or a declared short-lived child branch. Never omit branch on GitHub write operations.

active_work.goal: Complete AgentOS Core v0.1 as the canonical cross-session execution path: scoped external clients attach to deterministic durable context, submit bounded capabilities to the Oracle native node, and receive receipts without GitHub Actions acting as the task executor.
current_findings: Oracle now runs persistent agentos-control-plane.service and agentos-node.service; the native node leases Canonical IR tasks and completes receipts without GitHub Actions being the executor.
Session A -> task -> Oracle execution -> receipt -> Session B attach continuity is proven against the durable Control Plane store.
The public ONE/Core network edge is proven from an external GitHub-hosted runner using a short-lived scoped AgentOS client token; the token was revoked after the proof.
Client credentials are stored only as SHA-256 digests and support expiry, revocation, permissions, project allowlists, and capability allowlists; runtime lease/complete APIs remain root-only.

agentos.project.inspect is a real native capability gated by an Oracle-local project registry; LeopardCat inspection returned HEAD f44db405678cd54ce42b944e71a37de033ed8234 from executor oracle-core-node.
Context Compiler v0 is deterministic rather than model-generated. /v1/attach now returns agentos.execution-context/v0.1 with active goal, findings, next actions, latest task, branch and write policy.
A blind fresh-session attach with history=none successfully recovered the canonical AgentOS goal, next action and integration branch using durable state alone.
agentos.project.test is now a real native capability. Tasks may select only an administrator-defined profile name; task-supplied argv/command fields are ignored.

Oracle successfully executed the allowlisted agentos-core/core-v01 test profile and returned a succeeded receipt from executor oracle-core-node at native Core SHA 3cd3e177311f90592a51bd5e68c0909be871dd20.

The prior development context had become stale even though the Context Compiler worked correctly. Canonical context freshness is therefore part of the Master Experience Floor, not merely context transport.
WorkspaceGuard and the bounded Antigravity relay remain relevant for interactive/local executor integration, but they are no longer blockers for the Core attach/task/receipt execution plane.
feature/distributed-agentos-runtime remains the sole canonical vNext continuation line; experimental writes to main remain denied.
next_actions: Prove an external least-privilege client can submit agentos.project.test for only agentos-core/core-v01 through the public Core edge and receive an oracle-core-node receipt, then revoke the token.
Add an explicit freshness contract to execution_context so attached agents can detect stale canonical development context instead of silently trusting it.
Separate bootstrap/deployment responsibilities from normal AgentOS execution so GitHub Actions is clearly CI/deploy infrastructure rather than an execution dependency.

Wire a real weak interactive executor adapter (Antigravity or another bounded executor surface) to consume the same attach execution_context and emit receipts, then repeat the blind Master Experience Floor experiment.
Preserve the new Core v0.1 evidence in the AgentOS research record and update the paper/chronology after the external native-test edge and weak-executor proof are complete.

main.notes: Do not add further experimental work.

feature/distributed-agentos-runtime.notes: Canonical continuation point for current work.
